Nergal.fact: According to a hymn from the reign of Ishme-Dagan, dominion over the land of the dead was bestowed upon Nergal by his parents, Enlil and Ninlil. He was believed to decide fates of the dead the same way as Enlil did for the living.

Nergal.fact: In that capacity he was called Lugal-silimma, "lord of peace".

Nergal.fact: Two gods with names similar to Erra who were also associated with Nergal were Errakal and Erragal. It is assumed that they had a distinct origin from Erra.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: The city itself was sometimes called "Kutha of Sumer".

Nergal.fact: Her name is assumed to have its origin in a Semitic language, but both its meaning and Laṣ' character are unknown.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: Based on the Weidner god list, Wilfred G. Lambert proposes that she was a medicine goddess.

Nergal.fact: Couples consisting of a warrior god and a medicine goddess (such as Pabilsag and Ninisina or Zababa and Bau) were common in Mesopotamian mythology.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: Her name is homophonous with Mami, a goddess of birth known for example from the Nippur god list, leading some researchers to conflate them.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: Multiple meanings have been proposed for her name, including "oath" and "frost" (based on a similar Akkadian word, mammû, meaning "ice" or "frost").

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: It is possible she was introduced in _____ alongside Erra
Nergal.fact: It is possible she was introduced in Kutha alongside Erra. In at least one text, a description of a New Year ritual from Babylon during which the gods of Kish, Kutha and Borsippa were believed to visit Marduk (at the time not yet a major god), both she and Laṣ appear side by side as two separate goddesses.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: She is otherwise only known from personal names and a single offering list from Old Babylonian Mari.

Nergal.fact: He was an underworld god and is mostly known from personal names from the Ur III and Isin-Larsa periods.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: There is also clear evidence that he was regarded as Tadmushtum's husband.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: He points out that it is also not impossible that _____ only developed as a distinct deity at a later point in time
Nergal.fact: Two possible explanations have been proposed: Aštabi and Kumarbi. Gernot Wilhelm concludes in a recent publication that the identification of Nergal in the early Urkesh inscriptions as Kumarbi is not implausible, but at the same remains impossible to conclusively prove.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: However, other identities of the deity identified by this moniker have been proposed as well, with _____ instead identifying him as Ugur

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: According to _____ it cannot be established whether this indicates an equation with either the third millennium BCE god Kamish known from the Ebla texts, or the Iron Age god Chemosh from Moab
Nergal.fact: According to Wilfred G. Lambert it cannot be set up whether this indicates an equation with either the third millennium BCE god Kamish known from the Ebla texts, or the Iron Age god Chemosh from Moab.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: A secondary name of the E-Meslam was E-ḫuškia, "fearsome house of the underworld".

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: It is already attested in documents from the reign of _____, on whose orders repair work was undertaken there
Nergal.fact: It is already attested in documents from the reign of Shulgi, on whose orders repair work was undertaken there.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: Later monarchs who also rebuilt it include Apil-Sin, _____, Ashurbanipal and Nebuchadnezzar II
Nergal.fact: Later monarchs who also rebuilt it include Apil-Sin, Hammurabi, Ashurbanipal and Nebuchadnezzar II.

Nergal.question: It continued to function as late as in the _____ period
Nergal.fact: It continued to function as late as in the Seleucid period.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: Its precise location is not known, but it has been established that it was to the west of _____
Nergal.fact: Its precise location is not known, but it has been set up that it was to the west of Marad.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: In this city, he could be referred to as _____-Apiak
Nergal.fact: In this city, he could be called Lugal-Apiak.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: While absent from _____ in the Akkadian period, later he rose to the status of one of the most major gods there
Nergal.fact: While absent from Assyria in the Akkadian period, later he rose to the status of one of the most major gods there. Tarbiṣu was a particularly important Assyrian cult center of both Nergal and his wife Laṣ.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: His temple in this city, originally built by _____, also bore the name E-Meslam
Nergal.fact: His temple in this city, originally built by Sennacherib, also bore the name E-Meslam.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: This changed during the reign of Shulgi, the second king from the _____ of Ur
Nergal.fact: This changed during the reign of Shulgi, the second king from the Third Dynasty of Ur.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: He appears for the first time in documents from _____ in this period
Nergal.fact: He appears for the first time in documents from Uruk in this period. Anam of Uruk built a temple dedicated to him in nearby Uzurpara during the reign of Sîn-gāmil.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: Anam of Uruk built a temple dedicated to him in nearby _____ during the reign of Sîn-gāmil
Nergal.fact: Anam of Uruk built a temple dedicated to him in nearby Uzurpara during the reign of Sîn-gāmil.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: A temple bearing this name was rebuilt by Kudur-Mabuk at one point.

Nergal.question: It shared its name with a temple of Nanaya located in _____
Nergal.fact: It shared its name with a temple of Nanaya in Kazallu.

Nergal.fact: He could also be called the tutelary god of Marad, though this city was chiefly associated with Lugal-Marada.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: Offerings or other forms of worship are also attested from Dilbat, Isin, Larsa, Nippur and Ur. Temples dedicated to him also existed in both Isin and Nippur, but their names are not known.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: He is one of the gods considered to be "pan-_____" by modern researchers, a category also encompassing the likes of Teshub, Shaushka or Nupatik
Nergal.fact: He is one of the gods considered to be "pan-Hurrian" by modern researchers, a category also encompassing the likes of Teshub, Shaushka or Nupatik. He is already attested in the inscriptions of two early Hurrian kings of Urkesh, Tish-atal and Atal-shen.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: He is already attested in the inscriptions of two early _____ kings of Urkesh, Tish-atal and Atal-shen
Nergal.fact: He is one of the gods considered to be "pan-Hurrian" by modern researchers, a category also encompassing the likes of Teshub, Shaushka or Nupatik. He is already attested in the inscriptions of two early Hurrian kings of Urkesh, Tish-atal and Atal-shen.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: May the god _____ protect this temple
Nergal.fact: May the god Lubadaga protect this temple. Who destroys it, [him] may Lubadaga destroy.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: Who destroys it, [him] may _____ destroy
Nergal.fact: May the god Lubadaga protect this temple. Who destroys it, [him] may Lubadaga destroy.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: May the mistress of _____, the sun-god, and the weather-god [...] him who destroys it
Nergal.fact: May the mistress of Nagar, the sun-god, and the weather-god [...] him who destroys it.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: The sun god and the weather god in this inscription are most likely _____ and Teshub
Nergal.fact: The sun god and the weather god in this inscription are most likely Hurrian Shimige and Teshub.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: Let Shamash and Ishtar destroy the seeds of whoever removes this tablet. Giorgio Buccellati in his translation quoted above renders the names of the other deities invoked as Shamash and Ishtar, but according to Alfonso Archi the logograms dUTU and dINANNA should be read as Shimige and Shaushka in this case.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: These include _____, referred to as the "City of the Gods", which was located near modern Kirkuk, as well as Ḫilamani, Tilla and Ulamme, where an entu priestess dedicated to him resided
Nergal.fact: These include Arrapha, called the "City of the Gods", which was located near modern Kirkuk, as well as Ḫilamani, Tilla and Ulamme, where an entu priestess dedicated to him resided.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: The time of original composition is uncertain, with proposed dates varying from _____ to Middle Babylonian times
Nergal.fact: The time of original composition is uncertain, with proposed dates varying from Old Babylonian to Middle Babylonian times.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: Whether a _____ original existed is unknown, and the surviving copies are all written in Akkadian
Nergal.fact: Whether a Sumerian original existed is unknown, and the surviving copies are all written in Akkadian.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: However, he ignores one of them, and has sex with _____
Nergal.fact: After Nergal fails to pay respect to Ereshkigal's sukkal Namtar during a feast where he acts as a proxy of his mistress, who cannot leave the underworld to attend, she demands to have him sent to the underworld to answer for it. However, he ignores one of them, and has sex with Ereshkigal.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: After six days he decides to leave while _____ is asleep
Nergal.fact: However, he ignores one of them, and has sex with Ereshkigal. After six days he decides to leave while Ereshkigal is asleep.

Nergal.subject: International Relations

Nergal.fact: A colophon indicates that it was compiled by a certain Kabti-ilani-Marduk, which constitutes an uncommon of example of a direct statement of authorship of an ancient Mesopotamian text.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: Through trickery he manages to convince _____ (portrayed as a ruler past his prime, rather than as a dynamic hero, in contrast with other compositions) to leave his temple
Nergal.fact: Through trickery he manages to convince Marduk (portrayed as a ruler past his prime, rather than as a dynamic hero, in contrast with other compositions) to leave his temple. However, Marduk returns too soon for Nergal to successfully start his campaign, and as a result in a long speech he promises to give other gods a reason to remember him.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: As a result of his declaration (or perhaps because of _____'s temporary absence), the world seemingly finds itself in a state of cosmic chaos
Nergal.fact: Through trickery he manages to convince Marduk (portrayed as a ruler past his prime, rather than as a dynamic hero, in contrast with other compositions) to leave his temple. However, Marduk returns too soon for Nergal to successfully start his campaign, and as a result in a long speech he promises to give other gods a reason to remember him.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: However, _____ eventually manages to bring an end to the bloodshed
Nergal.fact: However, Ishum eventually manages to bring an end to the bloodshed. Ishum's war is described in very different terms to Nergal's, and with its end the period of instability comes to a close.

Nergal.subject: International Relations
Nergal.question: In the surviving fragments _____ unsuccessfully pleads with him to be released to avoid being put to death for his crimes at the orders of Marduk
Nergal.fact: The myth Enmesharra's Defeat, only known from a single, heavily damaged copy from the Seleucid or Parthian period, casts Nergal as the warden of the eponymous antagonist and his seven sons, the Sebitti, presumably imprisoned in the underworld. Non-Aligned Movement.fact: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) is a forum of 121 countries that are not formally aligned with or against any major power bloc. The movement originated in the aftermath of the Korean War, as an effort by some countries to counterbalance the rapid bi-polarization of the world during the Cold War, whereby two major powers formed blocs and embarked on a policy to pull the rest of the world into their orbits. Non-Aligned Movement.fact: One of the quotations within the Declaration is "Peace can not be achieved with separation, but with the aspiration towards collective security in global terms and expansion of freedom, as well as terminating the domination of one country over another".  According to Rejaul Karim Laskar, an ideologue of the Congress party which ruled India for most part of the Cold War years, the Non-Aligned Movement arose from the desire of Jawaharlal Nehru and other leaders of the newly independent countries of the third world to guard their independence and sovereignty "in face of complex international situation demanding allegiance to either two warring superpowers".  The movement advocates a middle course for states in the developing world between the Western and Eastern Blocs during the Cold War.  The phrase itself was first used to represent the doctrine by Indian diplomat V.  Krishna Menon in 1953, at the United Nations. Non-Aligned Movement.question: In its efforts to advance _____ interests, the movement has stressed the importance of cooperation and unity amongst member states
Non-Aligned Movement.fact: Since the end of the Cold War, the Non-Aligned Movement has felt forced to redefine itself and to reinvent its purpose in the new world-system.  A major question has been whether any of its foundational ideologies, principally national independence, territorial integrity, and the struggle against colonialism and imperialism, apply to contemporary issues.  The movement has emphasized its principles of multilateralism, equality, and mutual non-aggression in attempting to become a stronger voice for the Global South, and an instrument that can promote the needs of member-nations at the international level and strengthen their political leverage when negotiating with developed nations.  In its efforts to advance Southern interests, the movement has stressed the importance of cooperation and unity amongst member states.  However, as in the past, cohesion remains a problem, since the size of the organization and the divergence of agendas and allegiances present the ongoing potential for fragmentation.  While agreement on basic principles has been smooth, taking definitive action vis-à-vis particular international issues has been rare, with the movement preferring to assert its criticism
